edges.note: Descentralización y coordinación distribuida pueden compararse; no implican identidad entre teoría política y arquitectura técnica.
Cooperación como patrón social y coordinación de componentes; analogía, no equivalencia.
Crítica de autoridad y evaluación de justificaciones; no asumir que una postura política determina la verdad.
Materialismo y educación científica aparecen en autores clásicos; tratar como posiciones históricas debatibles.
Autoorganización como concepto común en sistemas sociales y técnicos.
Observation and evidence connect scientific practice to philosophical accounts of knowledge.
Biological accounts of cooperation can inform social analysis without reducing social institutions to biology.
Specialization can increase interdependence while also creating coordination and power questions.
Political-economic traditions disagree about property, markets and authority; preserve disagreement rather than flattening it.
Capitalism is a central object of political-economic analysis.
Abolitionist writing links emancipation to freedom and rights.
Narratives can stage ethical conflicts; fiction is not empirical evidence by itself.
Ecological systems and social/technical systems can share tools of systems analysis, not identical mechanisms.
Democratic legitimacy and concentrated authority can be in tension; relation does not imply a single conclusion.
Class and gender analyses can intersect while remaining distinct dimensions.
Scientific claims and political judgments require different kinds of justification.
Historical interpretation depends on evidence, provenance and competing explanations.
